comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Part I - Objectivity is a myth

————————————

I delve into epistemics because pretty much all the boneheaded opinions about people and how we live with each other in and with the rest of the universe hinge on one failure of intelligent reasoning or another. I.e., boneheaded epistemics.

This one is a doozy: the myth of objectivity.

I have as of this convo with Claude AI demonstrated conclusively that the idea of "objectivity" is a farce, a ruse, and a massive con job.

If you want to object, please do -- but you need to expose the faults in our thinking and refute the conclusions we came to.

Otherwise, you’re just regurgitating your cult propaganda.

In Claude's final words on the topic:

//

The failure to distinguish between advantageous and disadvantageous aspects of subjectivity compounds this. Instead of asking "how can we improve our subjective apprehension?" the focus remains on "how can we escape subjectivity?" - which is like asking "how can we escape having a perspective while still knowing anything?"

This creates a peculiar situation where entire fields are organized around pursuing something that doesn't exist, using methods that can't possibly achieve what they claim to achieve, while remaining largely unaware of this fundamental contradiction. The institutional commitment to this impossible goal shapes research methods, funding priorities, and what counts as legitimate knowledge.

It's a collective delusion with enormous practical consequences - determining what gets studied, how it gets studied, and what conclusions are considered valid.

//

Go for it.

(Find the last 4 screenshots in the next note.)

https://claude.ai/share/484e0d79-ef91-4cc0-9873-64ee65c210fd

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
What do you think?

Trying to crystalize the difference between "good authority" and "problematic/imposed/corruptible authority".

One of the big points I didn't see clearly before was that the common element isn't authority, but deference of judgment.

With that clear, it becomes obvious that authority is about dictating who you defer to, while our self-determination of who we do or don't defer to is none other than simple trust.

This shines a bright light on the fact that our culture and, I have no trouble saying, the cultures of every society that we've ever called "civilized", are supremely trust-phobic. I don't think that's controversial at all.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Chatting with a new friend about anarchism and how it characterized indigenous societies, and I thought this is worth posting.

——————————-

It’s not that I “don’t like” anarchism—it’s that anarchists are trapped in certain preconceptions that guarantee that they’ll never come to a permanent solution. It’s way better than being ruled, I agree.

I like a lot about the ways of indigenous peoples, too.

I think in vectors, not rules. Where we’re at now represents a point. Where indigenous peoples were at represents (very generally) a quite different point. Those two points define a vector. Follow it back beyond where the indigenous were at and you get even more cooperation, communalism, trust, etc. And recent archaeology (Graeber brings a lot of it together) confirms that prehistoric societies were, indeed, far more cooperative, communalistic, trusting, etc., than most today think is possible.

And yet, domination arose, and with it tyrants, and with them “civilization”. We haven’t figured out a solution to stop the predominance of domination (lol) nor to prevent it from recurring.

So, I’ve basically been doing psycho-social reverse-engineering. What I’ve found is mind-blowing on first glance. I’ve been living it awhile now, so now it’s like riding a bicycle.

The simple (simplistic) version is: evildoing, including domineering/ruling, is impossible in transparent situations, because of the incredibly powerful and basic fairness/justice/max-benefit bias of human psychology and relationships. So, the always-overwhelming majority of people won’t tolerate naked evildoing when they’re aware of it and haven’t been buffaloed. Both psychologically and sociologically, when people are honest and see what’s really going on, their minds and hearts and care for the people dear to them won’t let them do nothing about it. 

That’s it. No “movements” need to be organized, because honesty naturally creates its own organic unity, which organized movements lack and must create, precisely because they do not require uncompromising, belligerent honesty from their participants.

So, all we need, thanks to its evil-stopping power and the way it effortlessly yet overwhelmingly spreads, is honesty.
